items.title: Lisa Parrott interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 22, 2021
items.q: Sometimes we were transcribing Bird together

ctx.x: Whoa that’s very interesting. And I know I’m one of those people that always tries to make sense of things I hear, like gamelan music or — and I try to put it in a context that it doesn’t belong. And then I get aggravated because I can’t find one or something.

Right. And then a lot of like West African music, they don’t even have a concept of one. You know like they don’t think in numbers. And that’s — Steve Coleman was coming out of that concept. He used words like short and long. He didn’t use numbers. And I think that was extremely good for me because even though he I don’t know how can I explain this — the times we hung out together it wasn’t really just a teacher-student. We were just doing stuff together. Sometimes we were transcribing Bird together and I’d be…
That’s okay because I’m going to jump in with a quote about one of your tunes called “Gargoyle.” Okay.
